Sara and Nikhil — looping Legal in with suggested edits. I reviewed ACME_redline_v3.docx and propose the following redline language and constraints (high level):

1) Uptime target: we can accept a 99.9% monthly uptime commitment measured on a 30-day rolling window for hosted API. For Dedicated deployments we will provide availability targets in the SLA but exclude customer-managed infra from the calculation.

2) Maintenance windows: Planned maintenance to be performed with >= 72 hours notice. A monthly "blackout" of 2 hours is unusually restrictive for platform upgrades; suggest defining "maintenance window" as: up to 6 hours of planned maintenance per calendar month (scheduled in 2-hour blocks) and an explicit carve-out for critical security patches with 24-hour notice. Language: "Planned Maintenance means work reasonably required to maintain service security and integrity; Redwood will provide >=72 hours notice for non-critical Planned Maintenance and 24 hours for Critical Maintenance."

3) Response & Restore: Recommended compromise on response times — initial acknowledgement (P1) within 15 minutes (on-call triage), target time-to-restore for P1: 4 hours for most incidents; we cannot commit to a universal 2-hour restore across all incident types and scales. We request engineering confirmation on achievable restore windows per deployment.

4) Service credits: propose a non-cumulative credits model with a monthly cap equal to 50% of the monthly invoice for the affected service. Credits to be calculated on a pro rata basis tied to measured downtime buckets (example language included in attached doc).

5) Escalation & SOC2: We will provide a named escalation path and SOC2 Type II summary. Full SOC2 report access can be made available under an NDA; we'll include an SOC2 attestation reference in the Order Form.

I've attached legal_redline_sla_trackchanges.docx with inline language for your counsel. Please note: legal redlines above assume engineering confirms the restore/measurement approach in measurement_spec.xlsx.

Lauren Bishop

Subject: Re: Proposed Order Form SLA redlines — ops feasibility notes

Quick ops note on feasibility and suggested language we can commit to:

- Measurement: We measure availability at the customer route level in 1-minute granularity and report on 5-minute intervals for SLA calculation. Using a 30-day rolling window (as Legal suggested) is fine. See measurement_spec.xlsx for metric definitions.

- Uptime / Credits: 99.9% monthly for hosted API is feasible. For Dedicated, we need to exclude third-party infra and customer network outages from measurement.

- Response & Restore: P1 initial acknowledgement within 15 minutes (on-call triage) — we can accept that. Restore targets: recommend we commit to a 4-hour target for most P1 incidents, with an exception for region-wide outages (where we will commit to best-effort and expedited priority routing). For Dedicated customers, we can offer narrower SLAs (including faster RTO) if they purchase a higher support tier.

- Maintenance windows: We can support Planned Maintenance as 6 hours per calendar month with notifications >=72 hours. For true emergency security fixes we will aim for 24-hour notice but reserve the right to apply emergency patches with minimal notice.

Action items: Lauren — if legal is comfortable with the 4-hour P1 restore language and the non-cumulative credit cap at 50% monthly, we'll finalize the tracked Order Form. Nikhil — I can prepare the clean Order Form for signature once legal confirms.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
